1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) covers with the general aspects and methods of measurements of the parameters of piezoelectric ceramic materials. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 The following terms and definitions shall apply in addition terms and definitions given in IS : 1885 ( Part 44 )-1978t. to the

2.2 Piezoelectric Ceramic Element - Ceramic element which is fabricated and designed for specific transducer requirements with given geometric shape, size and orientation with respect to poling axis.

IS : 11014 ( Part 1 ) - 1984 2.3 Dielectric Constant ( K: ) The ratio between the charge stored the

on an electroded slab of material brought to a given voltage and charge stored on a set of identical electrodes separated by vacuum.

2.4 Dissipation Factor ( tan 6 ) - The power loss of the capacitor divided by the reactive power of the capacitor at a sinusoidal voltage to specified frequency. 2.5 Poling piezoelectric 2.6 Poling poling. A process of alignment of the dipoles material by applying strong dc field. The axis alon g which of the domains of for

2.7 Piezoelectric Charge Constant ( d ) - (a) Short circuit charge density developed per unit applied stress, and (b) Strain developed per unit applied field at constant stress. 2.8 Piezoelectric Voltage Constant (g ) - (a) Open circuit field developed for a given applied stress, and (b) Strain developed for a given charge density at constant stress. 2.9 Resistivity material. Resistance per unit length for unit cross section of the

2.10 Curie Temperature ( oc ) - The temperature above which the dielectric constant of the ferroelectric material obey the Curie-Weiss Law and piezoelectricity of the material disappear. 3. TYPE DESIGNATION materials covered by this standard are type

4.1 General

- For checking the properties/parameter of ceramic material it is necessary to making a test specimen of specified dimensions and shapes. Details of the test specimen shall be as specified in the relevant detail specification.
tests and routine be given relevant

4.1.1 ClassiJication of Tests - Type tests, acceptance tests, number of samples for each group of tests shall specification.

4.2 Density ( d ) - The dimensions of the ceramic disc shall be measured using vernier callipers, micromctcr or any such device within an accuracy of 0.05 mm and the mass shall be measured to an accuracy of 1 mg. The density may then be calculated using the expression: Density = mass/volume 5

In determining the frequency of maximum impedance, stray capacitance across the test specimen causes the maximum impedance to occur at Due to the high dielectric constants of a frequency which is too low. most piezoelectric ceramics, this error is negligible when the specimen is thin and extended electrode area. However, when the specimen is an end-electroded rod a serious error or may be introduced by stray capaTo avoid this error, a special shielded holder is used. citance. 5. MARKING
